title: Reader composition-root convergence v0
summary: Twenty-six rollback-sized slices convert the accepted exemplars into a reusable reader composition kernel, then stop at a parity contact-sheet checkpoint before closeout.

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
User-approved priority checkpoint placing composition convergence first.

verification: node --test focused reader compiler, runtime, route, and descriptor tests
allowedWork: Reader compiler page shells, build-time route manifests, inferred URL codecs, browser lifecycle services, piecewise scroll clocks, frame scheduling, runtime lesson descriptors, production renderer adapters, derived conformance and review descriptors, impact selection, closure, and bundle budgets.
Compatibility changes required for both accepted readers to consume the shared contracts, provided exact visual, semantic, URL, static-searchability, and responsive parity remains proven.
disallowedWork: Do not alter accepted equation or distribution semantics, choreography, visual policy, typography, colors, layout, attention behavior, searchable prose, or route meaning.
Do not add branch scheduling, structured algebra, advanced fraction composition, LLM mutation, new subjects, WebGL generalization, or editor redesign.
Do not introduce an abstraction used only by tests or only one production reader; integrate it in both readers or defer it.
Do not edit unrelated user-authored roadmap, thread, decision, or design documents.
goal: Converge accepted equation and distribution readers onto shared inferred page, route, URL, lifecycle, scheduling, adapter, conformance, review, and payload contracts without changing visible or semantic behavior.
commitCadence: Commit every independently verified rollback unit; combine analysis-only characterization with the first implementation slice it informs.
stopConditions: Stop if equation or distribution visual, semantic, URL, static-searchability, focus, review, or responsive parity regresses.
Stop if a shared abstraction cannot be consumed by both production readers without renderer-specific leakage or type erasure.
Stop if build routing becomes runtime-eager, unrelated adapters enter a reader bundle, or a route exceeds the approved payload baseline by more than five percent without explicit justification.
Stop if verification evidence is lost, an unexplained broad failure appears, or work expands into structured algebra, fractions, LLMs, new subjects, WebGL, or editor scope.
Stop after slice s25 for human review of equation and distribution parity contact sheets; do not execute s26 without new visual approval.
